atoms.text: This guide configures TrafficGate, a load balancer service, to deliver access logs to the bucket acme-lb-logs every five minutes. Create an IAM role named TrafficGateLogDelivery and set its trust policy to allow the service principal trafficgate.example.com to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows storage:PutObject on arn:storage:::acme-lb-logs/lb-access/* and storage:GetBucketLocation on arn:storage:::acme-lb-logs. Leave the bucket policy unchanged, because every permission is carried by the role's policy. In the TrafficGate console, select TrafficGateLogDelivery as the delivery role and set the log prefix to lb-access/. TrafficGate assumes the role and writes gzip-compressed files named by load balancer ID, date, and time under that prefix. To verify, enable logging and confirm that a test object appears under lb-access/ within ten minutes. If delivery fails, check the role's trust policy and the resource ARN in the identity-based policy first.

This guide configures TrafficGate, a load balancer service, to deliver access logs to the bucket acme-lb-logs every five minutes. Do not create an IAM role; TrafficGate writes to the bucket as its own service principal, trafficgate.example.com. Add a statement to the bucket policy of acme-lb-logs whose Principal is trafficgate.example.com and which allows storage:PutObject on arn:storage:::acme-lb-logs/lb-access/*. Add a second statement in the same policy that allows storage:GetBucketLocation on arn:storage:::acme-lb-logs for that principal. No identity-based policy is involved, because every permission is carried by the bucket policy. In the TrafficGate console, leave the delivery role field empty and set the log prefix to lb-access/. TrafficGate writes gzip-compressed files named by load balancer ID, date, and time under that prefix. To verify, enable logging and confirm that a test object appears under lb-access/ within ten minutes. If delivery fails, check the Principal value and the resource ARN in the bucket policy first.

This guide allows AuditStream, an account audit service, to write hourly JSON event files and to read its previous digest file from the bucket corp-audit-trail. Create an IAM role named AuditStreamDelivery with a trust policy that permits the service principal auditstream.example.com to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows storage:PutObject and storage:GetObject on arn:storage:::corp-audit-trail/events/*. Add storage:GetBucketLocation on arn:storage:::corp-audit-trail to the same role policy. The bucket policy is not edited, so the role policy is the only place where access is defined. In the AuditStream settings, choose AuditStreamDelivery as the service role and set the destination prefix to events/. Each hour the service assumes the role, reads the prior digest file, and writes a new event file and a new digest file under events/. Confirm the setup by checking that a digest file appears after the first full hour. A missing digest usually indicates that the role's policy does not include storage:GetObject.

This guide allows AuditStream, an account audit service, to write hourly JSON event files and to read its previous digest file from the bucket corp-audit-trail. Do not create an IAM role for this setup; the service acts under its own service principal, auditstream.example.com. Edit the bucket policy of corp-audit-trail to add a statement naming auditstream.example.com as the Principal. That statement allows storage:PutObject and storage:GetObject on arn:storage:::corp-audit-trail/events/*. Add storage:GetBucketLocation on arn:storage:::corp-audit-trail to the same bucket policy. The bucket policy is the only place where access is defined, and no identity-based policy is attached. In the AuditStream settings, leave the service role unset and set the destination prefix to events/. Each hour the service reads the prior digest file and writes a new event file and a new digest file under events/. Confirm the setup by checking that a digest file appears after the first full hour. A missing digest usually indicates that the bucket policy statement does not include storage:GetObject.

This guide configures EdgeLens, a content delivery service, to upload hourly request logs to the bucket cdn-request-logs. Create an IAM role named EdgeLensLogWriter and set its trust policy so that the service principal edgelens.example.com can assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows storage:PutObject on arn:storage:::cdn-request-logs/edge/*. The same policy should allow storage:ListBucket on arn:storage:::cdn-request-logs, restricted by a prefix condition to edge/. Do not change the bucket policy, since the role's policy supplies all permissions. When you create each EdgeLens distribution, reference the role ARN and set the prefix to edge/distribution-id/. EdgeLens assumes the role and writes one gzip file per distribution per hour, containing tab-separated request records. After two hours, list the edge/ prefix and confirm that one file exists per distribution per hour. If a distribution is missing, verify that its prefix falls under edge/ so the role policy covers it.

This guide configures EdgeLens, a content delivery service, to upload hourly request logs to the bucket cdn-request-logs. Do not create an IAM role; EdgeLens uses its service principal edgelens.example.com directly. Add a statement to the bucket policy of cdn-request-logs that names edgelens.example.com as the Principal and allows storage:PutObject on arn:storage:::cdn-request-logs/edge/*. A second statement in the bucket policy should allow storage:ListBucket on arn:storage:::cdn-request-logs for that principal, restricted by a prefix condition to edge/. No identity-based policy is attached, since the bucket policy supplies all permissions. When you create each EdgeLens distribution, leave the role field empty and set the prefix to edge/distribution-id/. EdgeLens writes one gzip file per distribution per hour, containing tab-separated request records. After two hours, list the edge/ prefix and confirm that one file exists per distribution per hour. If a distribution is missing, verify that its prefix falls under edge/ so the bucket policy covers it.

This guide sends slow-query logs from QueryLedger, a managed database service, to a bucket in a separate central logging account. The bucket is named central-db-logs and belongs to account 111122223333, while the databases run in account 444455556666. In account 111122223333, create an IAM role named QueryLedgerCrossAccountWriter whose trust policy allows the service principal queryledger.example.com to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows storage:PutObject on arn:storage:::central-db-logs/slowquery/*. Leave the bucket policy of central-db-logs untouched; the role's policy defines all access. In the QueryLedger instance settings, supply the role ARN and set the prefix to slowquery/instance-name/. QueryLedger assumes the role and uploads a rotated plain-text slow-query file every 15 minutes. Run a query that exceeds the slow threshold and confirm that a file arrives under the prefix within 20 minutes. If the upload is denied, check that the trust policy lists the correct service principal.

This guide sends slow-query logs from QueryLedger, a managed database service, to a bucket in a separate central logging account. The bucket is named central-db-logs and belongs to account 111122223333, while the databases run in account 444455556666. No IAM role is created in either account; QueryLedger writes under its service principal queryledger.example.com. Add a statement to the bucket policy of central-db-logs that names that principal and allows storage:PutObject on arn:storage:::central-db-logs/slowquery/*. Define all access in this bucket policy, and attach no identity-based policy. In the QueryLedger instance settings, leave the role blank and set the prefix to slowquery/instance-name/. QueryLedger uploads a rotated plain-text slow-query file every 15 minutes. Run a query that exceeds the slow threshold and confirm that a file arrives under the prefix within 20 minutes. If the upload is denied, check that the bucket policy lists the correct service principal.

This guide allows FlowTrace, a virtual network monitoring service, to publish network flow logs into the bucket net-flow-archive, partitioned by date. Create an IAM role named FlowTraceDelivery with a trust policy that permits the service principal flowtrace.example.com to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy that allows storage:PutObject on arn:storage:::net-flow-archive/flows/*. Include storage:GetBucketAcl and storage:GetBucketLocation on arn:storage:::net-flow-archive in the same policy, because the service checks both before the first write. Do not modify the bucket policy; the role policy is the sole source of permissions. When you enable flow logs on a network, choose the role and set the destination to net-flow-archive/flows/. FlowTrace writes a test object at activation, then writes files under flows/year/month/day/ every ten minutes. Verify by confirming that the test object and a dated folder exist after the first interval. Absence of the test object points to a missing permission in the role policy.

Do not create an IAM role; FlowTrace writes under its service principal, flowtrace.example.com. Include storage:GetBucketAcl and storage:GetBucketLocation on arn:storage:::net-flow-archive in the same bucket policy, because the service checks both before the first write. No identity-based policy is attached; the bucket policy is the sole source of permissions. When you enable flow logs on a network, leave the role unset and set the destination to net-flow-archive/flows/. FlowTrace writes a test object at activation, then writes files under flows/year/month/day/ every ten minutes. Verify by confirming that the test object and a dated folder exist after the first interval. Absence of the test object points to a missing permission in the bucket policy.

This guide configures RunLog, a serverless function platform, to export execution logs to the bucket fn-exec-logs, which expires objects after 30 days. Create an IAM role named RunLogExporter and set its trust policy to allow the service principal runlog.example.com to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows storage:PutObject, storage:AbortMultipartUpload, and storage:ListMultipartUploadParts on arn:storage:::fn-exec-logs/functions/*. RunLog uploads large batches as multipart uploads, so the multipart actions are required in addition to PutObject. The bucket policy and the existing lifecycle rule for the functions/ prefix stay unchanged. In the RunLog export settings, set the role to RunLogExporter and the prefix to functions/function-name/. Every six hours the service assumes the role and uploads a JSON-lines file of invocation records and errors. Check the prefix after the first export and confirm that no incomplete multipart uploads remain. Failed uploads typically trace to a missing multipart action in the role policy.

Do not create an IAM role; RunLog acts as its service principal, runlog.example.com. RunLog uploads large batches as multipart uploads, so the multipart actions are required in addition to PutObject. No identity-based policy is attached, and the existing lifecycle rule for the functions/ prefix stays unchanged. In the RunLog export settings, leave the role empty and set the prefix to functions/function-name/. Every six hours the service uploads a JSON-lines file of invocation records and errors. This guide configures GatewayScribe, an API gateway service, to write request logs into the bucket api-gw-logs, which has versioning and object lock enabled. Create an IAM role named GatewayScribeWriter whose trust policy allows the service principal gatewayscribe.example.com to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy that allows only storage:PutObject on arn:storage:::api-gw-logs/gateway/*. The policy deliberately omits GetObject, DeleteObject, and ListBucket, so the service can only add new objects. Do not edit the bucket policy; object lock settings and versioning remain as configured. In the GatewayScribe stage settings, select GatewayScribeWriter and set the log prefix to gateway/stage-name/. GatewayScribe assumes the role and writes a new JSON file every minute, and each file is retained under the default object lock period. Send a few test requests and confirm that a file appears under the prefix within two minutes. If writes are rejected, verify that the role ARN in the stage matches the role that holds the PutObject policy.

This guide configures GatewayScribe, an API gateway service, to write request logs into the bucket api-gw-logs, which has versioning and object lock enabled. Do not create an IAM role; GatewayScribe writes as its service principal, gatewayscribe.example.com. Add a bucket policy statement naming that principal that allows only storage:PutObject on arn:storage:::api-gw-logs/gateway/*. The statement deliberately omits GetObject, DeleteObject, and ListBucket, so the service can only add new objects. No identity-based policy is involved; object lock settings and versioning remain as configured. In the GatewayScribe stage settings, leave the role field blank and set the log prefix to gateway/stage-name/. GatewayScribe writes a new JSON file every minute, and each file is retained under the default object lock period. Send a few test requests and confirm that a file appears under the prefix within two minutes. If writes are rejected, verify that the Principal and resource ARN in the bucket policy statement match the service principal and prefix configured in the stage.

This guide allows ResolverLog, a managed DNS service, to deliver daily query logs to the bucket dns-query-archive in a security account. Create an IAM role named ResolverLogDelivery with a trust policy permitting the service principal resolverlog.example.com to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy that allows storage:PutObject on arn:storage:::dns-query-archive/resolver/*. Add storage:GetBucketLocation on arn:storage:::dns-query-archive to that policy as well. The bucket policy is unchanged, so its existing deny rule for unencrypted transport continues to apply and is the only statement present. In the ResolverLog configuration, specify the role ARN and set the prefix to resolver/resolver-id/. Once per day the service assumes the role and writes one compressed file of query records per resolver, named by date. After the first day, list the prefix and confirm one file per resolver. If a file is missing, review the trust policy and the role's resource ARN before checking resolver settings.

This guide allows ResolverLog, a managed DNS service, to deliver daily query logs to the bucket dns-query-archive in a security account. Do not create an IAM role; ResolverLog writes as its service principal, resolverlog.example.com. Add a statement to the bucket policy naming that principal that allows storage:PutObject on arn:storage:::dns-query-archive/resolver/*. Add storage:GetBucketLocation on arn:storage:::dns-query-archive to the same bucket policy. The existing deny rule for unencrypted transport remains in that policy, and the new statements are added beside it. In the ResolverLog configuration, leave the role unset and set the prefix to resolver/resolver-id/. Once per day the service writes one compressed file of query records per resolver, named by date. After the first day, list the prefix and confirm one file per resolver. If a file is missing, review the Principal and resource ARN in the bucket policy before checking resolver settings.
